item.title: Spain Hit by General Strike as Cost of Living Takes Center Stage Ahead of Elections
item.description: Demonstrators took to the streets of cities across Spain to join the country’s first general strike in 14 years, calling for measures to tackle the rising cost of living weeks before voters head to the polls.

item.title: The Global Economy Looks Vulnerable to an AI Bust
item.description: Some countries, especially in Asia, are heavily exposed to the U.S. data-center build-out.

item.title: Best High-Yield Savings Accounts of November 2026: Up to 5.00%
item.description: Beat average interest rates with one of these top high-yield savings accounts.

item.title: The Morning Risk Report: How Hackers Steal Millions in AI Computing Power
item.description: Plus: Jensen Huang affair revives push for chip restrictions and the U.S. has sued Lyft.

item.title: EU Takes Aim at Influencer Marketing, Deceptive Online Tactics With Revamped Rules
item.description: The European Union proposed new legislation to tighten its online consumer protection rules, targeting deceptive designs, influencer marketing and artificial intelligence.

item.title: Jensen Huang Affair Strains Taiwan’s Devotion to Its Hometown Hero
item.description: The Nvidia CEO’s affair has shaken Taiwan, his birthplace and a cornerstone of the AI chip industry he helped create.

item.title: Trump’s Plan to Import Russian Diesel Stalls on the High Seas
item.description: Several fuel tankers bound for the U.S. shifted course following difficulties finding buyers willing to accept the cargoes.

item.title: BOE Should Raise Key Rate to Around 5%, U.K. Economic Think Tank Says
item.description: Bank of England policymakers were set to move too slowly, the National Institute of Economic and Social Research said, urging them to raise the key rate to around 5% to tame inflation within three years.

item.title: Canada PM Carney Calls Stellantis Factory Sale ‘Unacceptable’
item.description: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said he’s prepared to use whatever legal and policy levers available to protect the roughly 2,000 workers affected.

item.title: U.K. Police Arrested a U.S. Army Soldier on Allegations of Spying for Russia
item.description: Plus, Wall Street is worried about interest rates again, and Anthropic’s founders are about to be worth billions.

item.title: Senior U.S. Soldier Is Arrested in U.K. Over Allegations of Spying for Russia
item.description: The 41-year-old man was assigned to a NATO rapid reaction command structure in the U.K.

item.title: U.S. Overture to Russia on European Security Sparks Alarm
item.description: U.S. officials said work on a Ukraine ceasefire must proceed alongside discussions about Europe’s future security arrangements.

item.title: U.K.’s Worst-Kept Secret: Who Was the Celebrity Accused of Preying on Teens
item.description: The David Walliams case, whose allegations he denies, has reignited debate over Britain’s strict libel laws and limits on press freedom.

item.title: Bank of England’s Lombardelli Signals Another Rate Rise Likely in Near Term
item.description: The central bank is likely to again raise its key interest rate in the near future, unless there is evidence of weakening inflation, the deputy governor said.

item.title: U.S., Iran Exchange Strikes on Islands as They Fight for Control of Strait
item.description: The U.S. and Iran are waging a fierce battle over control of the Strait of Hormuz, with both sides striking islands in the waterway in recent days.

item.title: The Morning Risk Report: Jensen Huang Doesn’t Believe in Succession Planning. It’s Become a Big Risk for Nvidia.
item.description: Plus: Washington probes Waymo over school-bus safety and U.S. balks at China’s demand for tightly scripted Trump-Xi-Putin summit.

item.title: Beijing Sees a Weakened Trump. It Risks Getting a Tougher Negotiator.
item.description: Plus, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang apologizes to employees and family, and Hong Kong activist Joshua Wong gets more prison time, for foreign collusion.

item.title: A Reined In Jensen Huang Is Nvidia’s Best Option
item.description: A more restrained chief would suit the chip giant well for the next phase of the AI boom.

item.title: Adnoc Gas Still Evaluating Options to Bypass Strait of Hormuz
item.description: The company has been examining ways to reduce its reliance on the strait—including an LNG export facility on the country’s east coast—its chief executive says.

item.title: Singapore Central Bank Rolls Out Gold-Vaulting Services
item.description: The Monetary Authority of Singapore is rolling out gold-vaulting services as part of efforts to make the city-state Asia’s top gold-trading hub.
